questions.q:
Carefully read the given passage and answer the questions that follow. Passage: In our approach to life, be it pragmatic or otherwise, a basic fact that confronts us squarely and unmistakably is the desire for peace, security and happiness. Different forms of life at different levels of existence make up the teeming denizens of this earth of ours. And, no matter whether they belong to the higher groups such as human beings or to the lower groups such as animals, all beings primarily seek peace, comfort and security. Life is as dear to a mute creature as it is to a man. Even the lowliest insect strives for protection against dangers that threaten its life. Just as each one of us wants to live and not to die, so do all other creatures.

options: burrow in the sand to avoid heat

questions.q: In a random arrangement of the letters of the word 'UNIVERSITY', what is the probability that two 1 's do not come together?
questions.solution:
The total number of arrangements of the letters of the word 'University' is $\frac{10!}{2!}$ as there are two i's. Regarding 2I's as one letter, number of ways of arrangement in which both I's are together $=9$ ! So, the number of ways in which 2I's are not together = $\frac{10!}{2!}-9$ !
Hence, the required probability
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{\frac{10!}{2!}-9!}{\frac{10!}{2!}} \\ & =1-\frac{2!9!}{10!}=\frac{4}{5} .\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of the equation $(x-a)(x-b)=c, c \neq 0$. Then the roots of the equation $(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)+c=0$ are
questions.solution:
The given equation $(x-a)(x-b)=c$ can be written as
$x^2-(a+b) x+(a b-c)=0$  ...(i)
$\because \alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the equation
$\left.\begin{array}{rl}\therefore \quad \alpha+\beta & =a+b \\ \alpha \beta & =a b-c\end{array}\right\}$  ...(ii)
If $\lambda$ and $\delta$ are the roots of equation
$\begin{aligned}(x-\alpha)(x-\beta)+c & =0 \\ x^2-(\alpha+\beta) x+(\alpha \beta+c) & =0 \\ \therefore \quad \lambda+\delta=\alpha+\beta & =a+b\end{aligned}$
and $\quad \lambda . \delta=\alpha \beta+c=a b$ by $\ldots(i i)$  
Clearly, the roots $\lambda$ and $\delta$ are $a$ and $b$.

questions.q: If the $10^{\text {th }}$ term of a GP is 9 and $4^{\text {th }}$ term is 4 , then what is its $7^{\text {th }}$ term?
questions.solution:
Let first term of G.P. is $a$ and common ratio $=r\because 10^{\text {th }}$ term of G.P. is 9
$\Rightarrow \quad a r^9=9$  ...(i)
and
$a r^3=4$  (ii)
Divide (i) by (ii)
$\frac{a r^9}{a r^3}=\frac{9}{4} \Rightarrow r^6=\frac{9}{4}\Rightarrow \quad\left(r^3\right)^2=\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2r^3=\frac{3}{2}$
Putting the value of $r^3$ in (i)
$a r^3=4a\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)=4 \quad \Rightarrow a=\frac{8}{3}7^{\text {th }}$ term $=a r^6=\frac{8}{3} \times \frac{9}{4}=6$.

$\begin{aligned} & \because \quad \tan \mathrm{A}-\tan \mathrm{B}=x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin \mathrm{~A}}{\cos \mathrm{~A}}-\frac{\sin \mathrm{B}}{\cos \mathrm{B}}=x \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\sin (\mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{B})}{\cos \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{B}}=x\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B} \quad \ldots(i)\begin{aligned} & \cot \mathrm{B}-\cot \mathrm{A}=y \\ & \frac{\cos \mathrm{~B}}{\sin \mathrm{~B}}-\frac{\cos \mathrm{A}}{\sin \mathrm{A}}=y\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}$  ...(ii)
From (i) and (ii) $x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}\begin{aligned} & \cot (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})=\frac{\cos (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})}{\sin (\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B})} \\ &=\frac{\cos \mathrm{A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{B}+\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}} \\ & {[\because x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}=y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}] }\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{x \cos \mathrm{~A} \cdot \cos \mathrm{~B}} \\ & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{\sin \mathrm{A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{B}}{y \sin \mathrm{~A} \cdot \sin \mathrm{~B}} \\ & =\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{y}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\tan A=1 / 2$ and $\tan B=1 / 3$, then what is the value of $4 \mathrm{~A}+4 \mathrm{~B}$ ?
questions.solution: $\tan \mathrm{A}=\frac{1}{2}, \tan \mathrm{~B}=\frac{1}{3}\tan (A+B)=\frac{\tan A+\tan B}{1-\tan A \cdot \tan B}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}}{1-\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3}}=\frac{\frac{5}{6}}{\frac{5}{6}}\begin{aligned} \tan (\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}) & =1 \\ \tan (\mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}) & =\tan \frac{\pi}{4} \\ \mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B} & =\frac{\pi}{4} \\ 4(\mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}) & =\frac{\pi}{4} \times 4 \\ 4 \mathrm{~A}+4 \mathrm{~B} & =\pi .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the maximum value of $3 \cos x+4 \sin x+5 ?$
questions.solution:
Since
$-\sqrt{3^2+4^2} \leq 3 \cos x+4 \sin x \leq \sqrt{3^2+4^2} \forall x\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow-5+5 \leq 3 \cos x+4 \sin x+5 \leq 5+5 \forall x \\ & \Rightarrow 0 \leq 3 \cos x+4 \sin x+5 \leq 10 \forall x\end{aligned}\therefore$ Maximum value of
$3 \cos x+4 \sin x+5=10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is the value of $\tan 15^{\circ} \cdot \tan 195^{\circ}$ ?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \tan 15^{\circ} \cdot \tan 195^{\circ} \\ & =\tan 15^{\circ} \cdot \tan \left(180+15^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\tan 15^{\circ} \cdot \tan 15^{\circ} \\ & =(2-\sqrt{3})(2-\sqrt{3}) \\ & =4-2 \sqrt{3}-2 \sqrt{3}+3 . \\ & =7-4 \sqrt{3} .\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\sin \theta=\cos ^2 \theta$, then what is $\cos ^2 \theta\left(1+\cos ^2 \theta\right)$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\because \begin{aligned} \because \sin \theta & =\cos ^2 \theta \\ \cos ^2 \theta\left(1+\cos ^2 \theta\right) & =\sin \theta(1+\sin \theta)\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sin \theta+\sin ^2 \theta \\ & =\cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta\end{aligned}=1 \quad\left[\because \sin \theta=\cos ^2 \theta\right]$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: What is $\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x}$ equal to?
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x}+\frac{1+\cos x}{\sin x} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 x+(1+\cos x)^2}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{\sin ^2 x+1+2 \cos x+\cos ^2 x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x\right)+1+2 \cos x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =\frac{2+2 \cos x}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\frac{2(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)} \\ & =2 \operatorname{cosec} x\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
What is the value of
$\tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\tan 63^{\circ}+\tan 81^{\circ} ?$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { We have, } \tan 9^{\circ}-\tan 27^{\circ}-\tan 63^{\circ}+\tan 81^{\circ} \\ & =\left(\tan 9^{\circ}+\tan 81^{\circ}\right)-\left(\tan 27^{\circ}+\tan 63^{\circ}\right) \\ & =\frac{1}{\cos 9^{\circ} \cdot \cos 81^{\circ}}-\frac{1}{\cos 27^{\circ} \cdot \cos 63^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{1}{\sin 9^{\circ} \cdot \cos 9^{\circ}}-\frac{1}{\sin 27^{\circ} \cdot \cos 27^{\circ}} \\ & =\frac{2}{\sin 18^{\circ}}-\frac{2}{\sin 54^{\circ}} \\ & =2\left[\frac{\sin 54^{\circ}-\sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 54^{\circ} \cdot \sin 18^{\circ}}\right] \\ & =2\left[\frac{2 \cos 36^{\circ} \cdot \sin 18^{\circ}}{\sin 18^{\circ} \cdot \cos 36^{\circ}}\right]=2 \times 2=4 .\end{aligned}$
